title: Modules & Packages
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Modules & Packages in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Module
items.text: A module is usually a Python file containing code such as functions, classes and variables.

items.heading: import
items.text: import loads a module so its names can be used by the program.

items.heading: from import
items.text: from module import name imports a selected name directly.

items.heading: Alias
items.text: An import alias gives an imported module or name a shorter local name.

items.heading: Package
items.text: A package is a structured collection of Python modules, usually arranged in directories.

items.heading: Why modules?
items.text: Modules help split a large program into smaller files and make reusable code easier to manage.

items.heading: Standard library
items.text: Python includes many ready-to-use standard library modules, such as json, math and datetime.

items.heading: pip
items.text: pip is the common Python package installer used to install packages from package indexes.

items.heading: Virtual environment
items.text: A virtual environment keeps a project’s installed packages isolated from other projects.

items.heading: __name__
items.text: The __name__ variable helps code know whether a module is being imported or run as the main program.

items.heading: Dependency versions
items.text: Pinning dependency versions can make an environment more reproducible.
